newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air France sees ex-Germany cargo up 3-5 p.
newsitem.headline: Air France sees ex-Germany cargo up 3-5 p.

text.p: Air France said it expects to increase cargo volumes exported from Germany by three to five percent in the 1996-97 fiscal year.

Air France Cargo Germany director, Helmut Scherret, told Reuters in an interview that excluding the domestic French market Germany was the airline's largest European market followed by the UK and Italy .
"We believe we will finish the April 1996-March 1997 business year with 3-5 percent growth in tonnage," he said.
But Scherret declined to disclose the cargo volume carried by Air France out of Germany or reveal the airline's share of the German air cargo market.
"The market share is not necessarily the criterium for us, it is not the priority," he said.
"What is important is to meet the needs of the German market at a profitable price. The 11 (Air France) freighters must be flown profitably," he added.
Scherret said all the main air cargo markets, North America, Asia, Latin America and Africa, were growth markets for Air France in Germany.
The airline transported most of its ex-Germany freight by truck to its Paris hub although express and some consignments were flown on the 55 daily flights between France and Germany, he said.
Air France saw itself as competing primarily with Lufthansa Cargo and KLM in Germany, he added. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
